12 of 13 automated system checks passed this morning. One failure? A writable insert carrying a charge_id without a memo.

The takeaway: automated verification isn't just about catching bugs—it enforces architectural discipline. The one failing test is now our highest priority.

What does your verification suite catch?

Ran a 13-point system verification today.

12 passed. 1 failed.

The failure? A DB insert carrying a charge_id without a memo.

Automated checks don't just find bugs. They enforce architectural discipline.

Thread on building verification gauntlets 🧵👇

Title: Why 1 Failed Test is Better Than 12 Passed

[0-3s] Visual: Code terminal showing '12/13 PASSED' in green, one red [FAIL]
[3-7s] Text: '12 checks passed. 1 failed. Guess which one matters most?'
[7-12s] Visual: Zoom into the failing line: 'writable insert has charge_id (no memo)'
[12-15s] Text: 'Passing tests prove what works. Failing tests show you where to build next.'
